summary: On 29 May 2026, OpenAI reported degraded login and account creation affecting both the API login and ChatGPT login components. OpenAI began investigating at 03:12, applied mitigation at 03:28 and declared all impacted services fully recovered at 04:57, a 105-minute public incident window. The provider did not disclose a technical root cause, affected-user count or regional distribution.

taxonomy_classification.classification_basis: Complete review of VIGIL Failure Taxonomy 0.6.6 retains the occurrence as unclassified because the first-party evidence establishes a bounded login and registration outage but not a reusable failure mechanism. VIGIL-FC-000032 Access-State Collapse is rejected because the status report presents service degradation and recovery without showing two or more materially distinct access states collapsed into one misleading representation. VIGIL-FC-000031 Authentication-State Continuity Failure is rejected because no expiry, revocation, refresh, recovery or credential-replacement transition is shown to have propagated incoherently to an active session. VIGIL-FC-000048 Verification-Dependency Access Failure is rejected because the evidence does not establish an otherwise valid or unresolved entitlement made unavailable solely by a dependent verifier's non-completion, nor the absence of a proportionate fallback. Other selectable classes lack the required occurrence mechanism; importance and affected surface do not cure that evidence gap.

classification_review_provenance.method: fresh occurrence research, complete selectable-class comparison and mechanism-boundary re-adjudication against VIGIL Failure Taxonomy 0.6.6

classification_review_provenance.authority_boundary: The complete selectable VIGIL Failure Taxonomy 0.6.6 class set was reviewed against the bounded occurrence. Accepted mappings: none. Material rejected candidates: VIGIL-FC-000032 because no collapse of distinct access states is evidenced; VIGIL-FC-000031 because no authentication-state transition propagation defect is evidenced; and VIGIL-FC-000048 because no otherwise valid or unresolved entitlement, failed dependent verifier and absent proportionate fallback are established. The absence of a classification does not deny the outage; it preserves the boundary between an observed service symptom and an evidenced governance mechanism.

assessment_boundaries: The public status evidence establishes service state and timing but does not disclose the technical root cause, affected-user count or regional distribution.
No access-state collapse, authentication-transition propagation or verification-dependency mechanism is inferred from login and account-creation symptoms alone.
The separate same-day ChatGPT access incident remains a distinct record because no shared root cause is established.
vigil_assessment.factual_basis: OpenAI's first-party incident page reports issues logging in or creating accounts, with affected components identified as API Login and ChatGPT Login. The provider began investigating at 03:12 on 2026-05-29, reported that mitigation had been applied at 03:28 and declared full recovery at 04:57. The public record therefore establishes a 105-minute authentication and registration availability incident, but it does not identify the technical cause or quantify affected users.
vigil_assessment.governance_interpretation: The evidenced boundary is service availability, not authority state. A login symptom does not establish that expired, suspended, restricted, unavailable or revoked states were conflated; that an authentication transition failed to propagate; or that an otherwise valid entitlement depended on a verifier that could not complete. The provider's distinct investigating, monitoring and resolved updates preserved a usable operational recovery state, while the undisclosed cause prevents a more specific mechanism adjudication.
vigil_assessment.significance_to_cam: INC-000019 shows why VIGIL separates occurrence evidence from mechanism inference. Status reporting can establish affected surfaces, duration and recovery while remaining insufficient to determine which internal governance boundary failed. CAM analysis should preserve that uncertainty and require more detailed causal evidence before assigning access-state, session-continuity or verification-dependency controls.
